doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Trying to name the Cheatham group's drummer, Iron Man
summary: Kimery and Brown try to explain a Detroit drummer nicknamed Iron Man, a name Young cannot hear clearly.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you remember who was in the band? [off mic]
She passed, no, he passed.
No, he…right. I think two years ago.
Jeannie is still living, but Jimmy passed. Oh, that was a nice group, man.
The drummer that we saw with Albert Mangelsdorff in Munich, called him ―Iron Man‖, from Detroit, he played with Jimmy and Jeannie…
I didn‘t understand, what you was talking to him, but…
I didn‘t understand either…[laughs]
He was the drummer from Detroit…
He was the drummer with who?
The drummer with Jimmy and Jeannie was from Detroit.
Yes.
And I can‘t think of his name but he…I saw him a few years back in Germany where he was playing a duet with trombonist Albert Mangelsdorff. He was known as ―Iron Man‖ also, that was his nickname…
You say he‘s ninety years old, almost?
His name was ―Iron Man‖…
Nickname.
Nickname ―Iron Man,‖ his nickname. His nickname was ―Iron Man.‖
I‘m not understanding that word, I wish I was.
―Iron Man.‖
Huh?
―Iron Man,‖ that‘s his nickname, ―Iron Man.‖ Like iron, like steel, iron.
Yeah, that‘s right…say that name again, say it again.
His nickname…
His nickname… Brown:…was ―Iron Man…Iron Man.‖
See, I can‘t get it, some words I just can‘t get.
Iron is like steel…
Iron Brown:…but iron, iron.
Iron.
―Iron…Man‖
Iron Man.
Yeah. Like steel, like steel…
Yeah.
Iron, ―Iron Man.‖ That‘s alright, that‘s alright.
That was the drummer in that band, is that what you‘re…
That‘s his nickname, yeah, that was his nickname.
Yeah.
And he was from Detroit.
